A Night to Remember chronicles one of the most famous tragedies in maritime history. The Titanic was the largest and most luxurious ship of its day. It was also deemed unsinkable because of its double-bottomed hull that was divided into 16 presumably watertight compartments, four of which could be flooded without endangering the ship’s buoyancy. # Titanic: A Night to Remember

April 14, 2025

|

6m

Share **Just one-third of the _Titanic_ ’s 2,200 passengers and crew survived the night of 14 April 1912. The Folio book of Walter Lord’s classic takes us back to those fateful events.** At 11.40 p.m. on the night of 14 April 1912, the ocean liner _RMS Titanic_ struck an iceberg in the Atlantic Ocean. Everyone thinks they know what happened next. But you don’t – you really don’t – until you read Walter Lord’s classic _A Night to Remember_ .

...

A _Titanic_ \-obsessed writer with an unerring eye for the telling detail, Lord spent hundreds of hours interviewing survivors.

...

# The story you thought you knew ...

Walter Lord's _A Night to Remember_ is the definitive account and the source for countless novels, plays and films, including James Cameron's _Titanic_ and is based on the testimony of survivors, as interviewed by author. In his minute-by-minute piecing together of events, Lord manages to convey both the detail and the sweep, the small sorrows and the all-embracing horror.
